key_insight: A fully discrete mixed-dimensional model couples porous flow, viscoelastic deformation and frictional fracture contact, with proven discrete well-posedness and error bounds.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports numerical analysis of fractured porous materials where fluid transport, deformation and fracture slip interact.
method: Couple matrix and fracture Darcy flow with linear viscoelastic matrix deformation.
Represent fractures as co-dimension-one interfaces with normal compliance and Coulomb friction.
Discretize using conformal finite elements in space and implicit Euler in time.
evidence_signal: The paper establishes discrete existence, uniqueness, stability and a priori error estimates, then compares computed numerical errors with theory in one numerical experiment.
watch_item: Validation described in the abstract is limited to one numerical experiment; broad applicability to complex fracture networks is not demonstrated there.
paper_title: Numerical analysis of coupled flow, deformation and frictional contact mechanics in a fractured porous medium
